notes: SHIP v1.14.403 - AISLE LIFECYCLE TRACE. INSTRUMENT ONLY, ZERO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE. Owner-directed after the physical-iPhone reproduction: tap OPEN AISLE, the correct 3D aisle opens, NO TOAST appears, the sheet closes itself, and the rack-detail screen underneath is revealed. WHY STATIC ANALYSIS COULD NOT FINISH THIS. Every path that should be able to close that sheet was checked and eliminated: forge3d_close() has exactly ONE caller in the entire file, the close button at :13107; showMode() dismisses only the profile sheet and the phase dock, never the aisle; #forge3d-sheet is a DIRECT CHILD of #app rather than of any page, so no Build or route re-render can destroy it; and unlike #ph-sheet, which carries onclick=if(event.target===this)phdock_close(), the aisle sheet has NO backdrop-close handler at all. The absence of a toast independently rules out the documented fallback: reh3d_fail() is the ONLY function that removes .is-3d to reveal the flat elevation, and it always toasts. So the close is invisible to reading the source and the app has to catch it in the act. THE OWNER SHOULD NOT HAVE TO READ A CONSOLE. This writes through the existing phantom_logErr into the existing phantom_crash_log ring, which means it is readable ON THE PHONE at SYS then ERRORS, with no Safari console, no cable, and NO NEW STORAGE KEY - a new key would have required M1 registry classification, and reusing the one existing door avoids that entirely. WHAT IS RECORDED, in order: OPEN_AISLE_CLICK, AISLE_OPEN_REQUESTED, AISLE_HOST_CREATED with the mount's measured width and height, ENGINE_ATTACH_STARTED, ENGINE_ATTACHED, FIRST_FRAME (one-shot), AISLE_PAUSED, AISLE_RESUMED, AISLE_TEARDOWN with a stack, AISLE_CLOSE_REQUESTED with a stack, AISLE_CLOSED_OBSERVED, UNDERLYING_ROUTE_REVEALED, AISLE_HOST_REMOVED. Every entry carries a state snapshot: sheet open flag, in-DOM flag, body.rd, mount child count, whether the rack host still has is-3d, the redesign mode, document.hidden, and the full RackEngine.report() attachment list - which is exactly the readout the owner was previously being asked to type by hand. HOW THE RING WILL NAME THE DEFECT. If AISLE_CLOSED_OBSERVED appears with NO AISLE_CLOSE_REQUESTED immediately before it, the close did not come through forge3d_close and no code in this file did it. If AISLE_TEARDOWN appears while the sheet is still open, the SCENE died rather than the sheet closing, and its stack names whoever called dispose - most likely RackEngine.releaseOthers() firing because another renderer registered. If AISLE_PAUSED appears right after ENGINE_ATTACHED, the .401 IntersectionObserver decided the host was not visible and stopped the loop, which has been the standing suspicion and is now measured rather than argued. If FIRST_FRAME never appears, the loop never ran a single tick. HONEST LIMIT, RECORDED IN THE CODE: a MutationObserver callback runs in its own microtask, so the stack captured there is the observer's and not the mutator's. That is precisely why forge3d_close is instrumented separately - the PRESENCE or ABSENCE of its entry is the discriminating fact, not the observer's stack. SAFETY: every hook is record-only and individually wrapped in try/catch, so a fault in the instrument can never alter the flow it measures. No route changed, no scene touched, no fallback added, no retry added, RACK SCENE LOCK untouched. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile clean x3, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4557/4557 delta 0, line endings unchanged all-LF, PRECACHE untouched, three-stamp lockstep. DEVICE-VERIFY: clear the service-worker cache, tap OPEN AISLE, let it fail as it did before, then open SYS then ERRORS and read the AISLE/ entries newest-first. No console needed.
